items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: Geechee didn't have a set style. He didn't copy anyone, but he did try to play solos in Tricky Sam style with Dewey. But he also played his own solos.

ctx.x: Well, it's still not, uh, note for note sitting around an hour and night long like some people out here nowadays. It's playing a series of riffs, it's the same thing. Just juggling riffs around that they picked out from somebody else. Well, what about Geechee Fields? Who do you think he sounded like?

You mean Geechee Robison? I mean Geechee Robison. I'm trying to write. That's a New York drama pop. I'm trying to write at the same time. Yeah, but here's the thing about Geechee. Geechee didn't have a set style. He didn't copy anyone, but he did try to play solos in Tricky Sam style with Dewey. But he also played his own solos.
Yeah, well if anything, you know, to me it sounds like he listened to maybe a Jimmy Harrison song.
